Marriage is (supposed to be) a contract. Contracts (are supposed to) have three features:

  • explicit terms. Both parties know exactly what they're getting from the contract, and what their responsibilities are

  • informed consent. Both parties agree to the terms.

  • enforcement. There are negative consequence to the party that breaks the agreement.

It used to be that the wedding vows represented the terms. Both parties could provide informed consent because they spoke the vows themselves. Enforcement was meted out by the community, before whom the vows were spoken, and was in the form of negative social consequences to the party that broke them.

But in modern marriage, the vows are just poetry. They are otherwise meaningless. The wedding is just a party.

And I thought this part of the post was particularly insightful: it is no longer possible for man to give informed consent. The actual contract is now in the form of volumes of court cases that he cannot begin to understand. Worse, enforcement of a broken contract doesn't actually punish the person who broke it. The bottom line is, don't get married. That's something MGTOW and The Red Pill seem to agree on.
